newsitem.title: UK: FOCUS - Dollar firm against yen, Euro bourses mixed.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS - Dollar firm against yen, Euro bourses mixed.

text.p: The dollar scored a 42-month high above 114 yen on Monday, as the Japanese currency weakened across the board, but could only hold steady against the mark.

Leading European bourses put on a mixed performance. A surprise takeover bid helped the London stock market, Europe's busiest, attempt to get back nearer to recent record levels in the morning but investors' enthusiasm later faded.
The Frankfurt bourse advanced by one percent, boosted by a stream of encouraging corporate news, but Paris slipped back after a more positive start.
Wall Street followed through on Friday's gains, with the Dow Jones industrial average adding around 20 points to 6,027 after gaining 14.54 on Friday.

Traders said a busy week for U.S. data could prompt caution on markets generally, given a common focus on the health of the American economy. The run of statistics will culminate in U.S. October jobs figures on Friday.

The yen suffered as Japanese investors kept on searching for higher-yielding investments abroad and amid uncertainty over the eventual political outcome after Japan's general election on October 20 left a hung parliament, market analysts said.
"Japanese investors are still showing a tremendous appetite for overseas assets," said Pat Magill, head of the corporate desk at Daiwa Europe.
"We probably won't see the end (of yen weakness) until Japan puts (interest) rates up," added Thomas Rayner, international economist at Societe Generale Strauss Turnbull.
Faltering Japanese economic growth, a further deterioration of its trade position and an expected bias towards easier fiscal and monetary policies all add up to a weaker yen, analysts said.
Compared with its advance against the yen, most of which it held at the end of the session, the dollar made little impression on the mark amid fading hopes for German rate cuts.

Elsewhere, the pound scaled a 16-month peak of $1.6145, hit 2.4590 marks, its strongest against the German currency since December 1995, and touched 184.35 yen, its highest against the yen since February 1993. But it slipped from its highs by the close.
Heavyweight blue chip companies including Daimler-Benz, BASF and Volkswagen led an advance which added more than one percent to the 30-share DAX index in Frankfurt.

Shares in Volkswagen rose nearly three percent after the government proposed repealing laws governing the car giant which analysts said would give the group more freedom and small shareholders more influence.

The London stock market reversed slight opening losses to head higher after a surprise bid for Northern Electric, later rejected by the utility. Northern Electric shares were up 120 pence at 650 pence, compared with the bid price of 630.
"We saw the bid lift the market," said one trader. "The market was going to be dull and drifting ahead of economic news this week but this has certainly lifted sentiment."

While London markets look ahead to the government budget in a month's time, this week's main economic diary entry in Britain is Wednesday's monthly monetary meeting between the finance minister and the governor of the Bank of England, although analysts expect no change in interest rates.
French shares weakened in modest volume, consolidating last week's gains ahead of U.S. data and next week's U.S. elections.
Lagardere fell nearly seven percent to 154.50 francs, after a good run in previous weeks, on growing unease about its planned takeover of Thomson.
CURRENCIES AT 1630 GMT
The dollar was trading around 1.5207 marks and 114.25 yen, compared with 1.5201 and 113.28 in late European business on Friday. It earlier hit a high of 114.40 yen.
STOCKS AT THE EUROPEAN CLOSE
London's FTSE 100 index finished up 2.9 points at 4,025.3.
Germany's DAX index ended bourse floor trade 29.61 ahead at 2,703.83 and showed little net change in later electronic trade.
In Paris the CAC-40 index closed down 12.04 at 2,150.39.
PRECIOUS METALS

Gold ended London trading at $383.35 an ounce after being fixed at $382.90 in the afternoon versus a morning setting of $382.80 and Friday's London close of $382.65. Silver edged up one cent to $4.93.
